newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan buys 115,800 tonnes of rice at tender.
newsitem.headline: Japan buys 115,800 tonnes of rice at tender.

text.p: The Japanese Food Agency said it bought 115,800 tonnes of rice at an import tender on Thursday.
It said it bought 50,000 tonnes from the United States, 30,000 from Australia and 35,800 from Thailand.
The average price was 67,823 yen per tonne, the agency said.

Under a 1993 General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade agreement, Japan agreed to gradually open its long-closed rice market and committed itself to importing 511,000 tonnes of rice during the fiscal year to the end of next March.
The Food Agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry, is the sole importer of rice.
So far this fiscal year, the Food Agency has bought only 39,500 tonnes, mainly from China and Australia. It bought the rice at the last tender in late July.
The latest import tender was delayed because of ample stocks and Japan's general election on October 20, industry officials said.
Some rice exporters, particularly Australia, expressed frustration at the delay.
